correctness.rationale: For a finite product of fields, vertices have nonempty proper support A; ordinary zero-divisor graph adjacency means disjoint supports. Nonzero annihilator supports are subsets of A^c and B^c, so weak adjacency requires choosing distinct annihilator coordinates, equivalent to |A^c∪B^c|≥2. For distinct support classes, the weak-minus-ordinary difference graph joins exactly intersecting supports; an individual class of size |A|≤t-2 is itself complete, whereas coatom classes are internally independent. Thus cliques are weighted intersecting support families, weight a^{|A|} for sizes≤t-2 (a=q-1≥2), weight 1 per coatom. Among families without singleton supports, every coatom can be added; complementary pairs of sizes 2 through t-2 contribute at most a^{max(|A|,t-|A|)}; choosing all >half supports and one from each complementary middle pair attains this bound because any noncomplementary half-sets intersect. A family with singleton {i} is bounded by full i-star, whose apparent singleton advantage over the coatom-complete choice is a-1. A complementary pair {i,j}, [t]\{i,j} has t≥5 and contributes gain at least a^{t-2}-a²≥a²(a-1)>a-1 to the nonsingleton choice, while all other complementary pair contributions are no smaller. Hence no singleton-family maximizes. Strict a>1 forces the larger support from every unequal-size complementary pair, all coatoms and exactly one half-set of every middle pair, proving the full equality classification and count a^{t(t-1)} times 2^{binom(t,t/2)/2} in even dimension. Independent SCIPY HiGHS MILP in integer support space returned globally optimal status and exact values 85,275,326,1491,1239 at (t,q)=(5,3),(5,4),(6,3),(6,4),(7,3), and independent enumeration verified all 2^10=1024 complementary middle choices for t=6; infinite claim follows from combinatorial inequalities, not these finite optimizations.

evidence: Wani resolves t=3,4 and gives bounds plus an explicit open exact clique question at t≥5; its refined upper bound can retain a singleton/coatom term, while the new proof excludes it for equal q≥3. Filmus weights all subsets by μ_p(A) without a coatom cap or forbidden full set.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest broad results do not imply the specific t≥5 parity formula and all equality cases without the new support/singleton comparison. A general weighted-intersection theorem could potentially be specialized but no checked exact covering formulation appears.

originality.rationale: Wani 2026 precisely introduced the same weak zero-divisor difference graph, proved the support reduction, determined small t=3,4 clique numbers, and posed exact general t≥5 as Question 6.11 with upper/lower bounds. The homogeneous q≥3 special family here is a substantive part of that open regime and the new strict singleton-star comparison removes the remaining coatom contribution gap; full equality classification and number of maximizing vertex-cliques also go beyond Wani. Filmus 2016 provides a broad weighted Ahlswede–Khachatrian theorem for full Boolean-lattice product measure; that weight differs crucially at coatoms and omits the full support, so it does not directly give the claimed ring graph theorem. No identical stronger theorem was identified; traditional weighted intersecting-family machinery may simplify the proof but does not erase this natural exact application.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed weighted intersecting-family theorem with a coatom-capped and top-deleted weight could subsume the equality classification as a corollary; the specific Wani question and same-object primary evidence make coverage less likely.
The proof uses q≥3 essentially for a=q-1>1; q=2 may have distinct maximizers. Unequal field orders require a separate weighted optimization and are unproved.
Finite MILP cases corroborate but do not constitute proof for all t and prime-power q.

final_claim: For every prime power q≥3 and t≥5, the weak zero-divisor difference graph of R=(F_q)^t has clique number t+Σ_{j=(t+1)/2}^{t-2} binom(t,j)(q-1)^j for odd t, and t+(1/2)binom(t,t/2)(q-1)^(t/2)+Σ_{j=t/2+1}^{t-2}binom(t,j)(q-1)^j for even t. All maximizing cliques consist of every support class strictly above half and ≤t-2, exactly one vertex from each coatom class, and for even t exactly one whole class from each complementary middle pair. Their number is (q-1)^{t(t-1)} times 2^{binom(t,t/2)/2} for even t.
limitations: Exact formula and complete maximizer classification only for R=(F_q)^t with equal q≥3 and t≥5, not q=2 equality cases, not arbitrary unequal factors or general finite rings.
